title: Metering & Measurement Language Guidance (Contracts)
author: Sofia Mendes
related_pages: Linear: PM-614 (Coordinate legal review of measurement language updates)
body:
## Purpose
This page provides approved contract language and negotiation guidance for **measurement and billing** for Redwood Inference products, including:
- Hosted API (usage-based, token- and request-level meters)
- Dedicated capacity (commit burn-down and usage attribution)
- Private deployments (license + support; may include usage reporting for overages/true-ups depending on order form)

It also outlines standard positions on **dispute windows**, **audit rights**, and treatment of **retries, failed requests, streaming disconnects, caching/batching, and rounding**.

**Audience:** Legal, Finance/RevOps, Sales Ops, AEs/CSMs (enablement only)

**Not legal advice for customers.** This is internal guidance. Use only the most recent approved language and involve Legal for redlines.

---

## Source of truth for meter definitions
For customer-facing definitions of meters and edge cases, do not re-invent descriptions in contracts.

**Default reference documents (internal):**
- Hosted API meter dictionary: **“Hosted API Meter Definitions v3”**
- Invoice mapping: **“Invoice line-item mapping to telemetry”**
- Rounding + streaming accounting decision: **ADR-027**

**Contract approach:**
1) Use a short, durable **Measurement & Billing** clause in the MSA.
2) Put product- and pricing-specific definitions in the **Order Form** / **Usage Schedule** (recommended) and reference Redwood documentation as “descriptive, non-binding” unless explicitly incorporated.

**Why:** Meter details evolve (e.g., new endpoints, model aliases, additional dimensions like request outcome). Contracts should remain stable while still giving customers clarity.

---

## Recommended structure (MSA + Order Form)
### 1) MSA
Include:
- Measurement authority and invoicing cadence
- Dispute window and process
- Limited audit right (billing records only)
- Treatment of taxes, late fees (if applicable), and suspension rights (if applicable)

### 2) Order Form / Usage Schedule
Include:
- Meter names and units (e.g., input tokens, output tokens, embeddings units, rerank units)
- Rates per unit and any included credits/allowances
- Any plan gating / eligibility (if a pricing experiment is involved, ensure the OF overrides)
- Time zone and billing period
- Dedicated: definition of “Committed Spend/Commit” and burn-down mechanics

---

## Approved MSA clause (default) — Measurement & Billing
**Use case:** Standard Hosted API usage-based billing and Dedicated usage attribution.

> **Measurement; Usage Records.** Fees may be based on Customer’s use of the Services as described in the applicable Order Form(s) (“Usage-Based Fees”). Redwood will measure Customer’s use of the Services using Redwood’s systems and usage telemetry generated by the Services (“Usage Records”). Usage Records will be used to calculate Usage-Based Fees and to generate invoices. Customer may access usage information through Redwood’s console or other reporting tools; such reports are provided for informational purposes and may differ from invoiced amounts due to timing, aggregation, or reporting configurations.
>
> **Invoicing.** Unless otherwise stated in an Order Form, Redwood will invoice Usage-Based Fees monthly in arrears. Rates, included usage, credits, and any minimum commitments are set forth in the applicable Order Form.
>
> **Disputes.** Customer must notify Redwood in writing of any good-faith dispute of an invoice within **thirty (30) days** of the invoice date and must provide reasonable detail supporting the dispute, including (as applicable) the impacted invoice, date range, organization/project identifiers, request identifiers, and any relevant logs. If Customer does not notify Redwood within this period, the invoice will be deemed accepted. The parties will work in good faith to resolve invoice disputes promptly. Customer will pay all undisputed amounts when due.
>
> **Audit (Billing Records Only).** No more than once in any twelve (12) month period, Customer may, at its expense, audit Redwood’s records relating solely to the calculation of Usage-Based Fees for Customer’s account for the prior twelve (12) months, by providing at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice and conducting the audit during Redwood’s normal business hours in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Redwood’s operations. Any auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement. Customer will promptly share the audit results with Redwood. This audit right does not provide access to Redwood’s source code, security controls beyond standard compliance materials, or other customers’ data.
>
> **Adjustments.** If an audit or the parties’ investigation determines that Redwood overcharged Customer, Redwood will issue a credit or refund for the overcharged amount. If Redwood undercharged Customer, Customer will pay the undercharged amount.

**Negotiation notes (Legal):**
- The “deemed accepted” language is important for close controls and prevents open-ended disputes. Avoid extending beyond 45 days without Finance sign-off.
- Keep the audit scoped to “records relating solely to the calculation of Usage-Based Fees” and prohibit source code access.

---

## Order Form / Usage Schedule language (Hosted API)
### A) Meter definitions (template)
**Add as a schedule/appendix to the Order Form.** Keep it short and align to v3 definitions.

> **Usage Metrics.** Customer will be billed based on the following usage metrics (each, a “Meter”):
> - **Input Tokens:** tokens submitted by Customer in requests to the text generation/chat endpoints.
> - **Output Tokens:** tokens generated by the Services in response to Customer requests.
> - **Embedding Units:** units measured per embedding endpoint request as described in the Service documentation.
> - **Rerank Units:** units measured per reranking endpoint request as described in the Service documentation.
> - **Requests (if applicable):** count of API requests to specified endpoints.
>
> **Measurement Details.** Usage is measured based on Redwood’s Usage Records. Meter definitions, including how tokens are counted across supported model families and endpoints, are described in Redwood’s product documentation.

**Guidance:**
- If the customer asks to bake a full meter dictionary into the contract, escalate to Legal + Engineering + Finance; strongly prefer a short schedule.
- If required, attach a PDF snapshot of the meter definitions with a date/version (see “Incorporating documentation” section below).

### B) Rounding + aggregation (template)
> **Aggregation and Rounding.** Usage may be aggregated across requests and may be rounded at the invoice line-item level as specified by Redwood’s billing system. Rounding practices are intended to be consistent within a billing period.

**Position:** We do not commit to “per-request rounding” in contracts. (See ADR-027.) If a customer insists on explicit rounding, involve Finance and Engineering; ensure feasibility and auditability.

### C) Streaming responses + disconnects (template)
> **Streaming Responses.** For streaming responses, usage is measured based on tokens generated and delivered prior to completion, cancellation, or disconnection. If a client disconnects or cancels, usage may include tokens generated up to the point the Services process the cancellation or disconnect.

**Position:** Avoid absolute statements like “never billed after disconnect” unless Engineering confirms current behavior for that endpoint/version. Prefer “up to the point the Services process the cancellation/disconnect.”

### D) Retries, timeouts, and failed requests (template)
> **Retries; Failed Requests.** Usage may be incurred for requests that are retried or that fail after processing begins (including, for example, due to customer-side timeouts, network interruptions, or invalid parameters detected after partial processing). Redwood may, in its discretion, issue credits for confirmed measurement defects or service errors pursuant to the applicable support terms.

**Internal note:** This is intentionally broad to cover partial processing and customer-initiated retries. Support will still apply the billing discrepancy triage runbook for case-by-case decisions.

### E) Caching/batching (template)
> **Caching and Batching.** Redwood may use batching, caching, quantization, or other optimization techniques to operate the Services. Such techniques may affect performance and internal resource consumption but do not change how Meters are calculated unless expressly stated in an Order Form.

**Rationale:** Prevent “you cached therefore you must charge less” arguments unless the commercial model explicitly includes “cached token” discounts.

---

## Dedicated: commit burn-down and attribution language
**Use case:** Customers want clarity on how usage applies against a commit and what happens with overages.

> **Committed Spend and Usage Attribution (Dedicated).** If the Order Form includes a committed spend or minimum monthly fee (“Commit”), the Commit will be invoiced as stated in the Order Form and will be applied against Usage-Based Fees incurred during the applicable period. Usage is attributed to the Dedicated deployment(s) identified in the Order Form (e.g., by deployment ID/cluster) and measured using Redwood’s Usage Records. If Usage-Based Fees exceed the Commit in a billing period, Redwood will invoice the excess at the rates in the Order Form. Unused Commit (if any) will expire at the end of the applicable period unless the Order Form expressly provides for carry-forward.

**Negotiation notes:**
- Avoid “rollover” by default; it complicates revenue and forecasting.
- If a customer requests carry-forward, require Finance approval and explicit language with limits (e.g., 1 month, capped percentage).

---

## Private: measurement language (if usage is referenced)
Many Private deals are license-based; usage language is only needed if there are overages, true-ups, or a hybrid (e.g., Private control plane + hosted failover).

> **Usage Reporting (Private).** To the extent the Order Form includes usage-based components or true-ups, usage will be measured using Redwood’s Usage Records from the applicable Private deployment(s) and reported through Redwood’s reporting tools or periodic exports. The parties will cooperate in good faith to validate usage measurement in the event of a dispute.

**Note:** If the Private environment is air-gapped/on-prem, confirm with Engineering what telemetry is available and whether “Usage Records” are generated locally, exported, or derived from customer logs.

---

## Dispute window guidance
**Standard:** 30 days from invoice date.

**Acceptable (with Legal + Finance alignment):** up to 45 days for strategic enterprise deals.

**Avoid:** 60–90+ days; open-ended dispute periods; “dispute pauses all payment obligations.”

**Operational dependency:** Support and Finance require timely disputes to reconcile against raw telemetry windows and retain audit evidence (see reconciliation methodology and close checklist).

---

## Audit rights guidance
### Default position
- Allow audit of **billing calculation records only**
- Limit to **1x per 12 months**
- Require notice, business hours, confidentiality, and non-interference
- Explicitly exclude source code and other customers’ data

### Common redlines and how to respond
- **Customer wants SOC2-style security audit rights embedded in billing audit clause:** separate the topics; offer compliance reports under NDA.
- **Customer wants third-party auditor with broad access:** restrict scope; require independent auditor; Redwood pre-approval not unreasonably withheld.
- **Customer wants audit if “material discrepancy suspected”:** you may allow earlier audit with written evidence, but keep frequency limits and scope.

---

## Incorporating documentation by reference (when required)
### Preferred approach (non-binding descriptive reference)
Use when customers want transparency but you need flexibility as meters evolve.

> **Documentation.** Redwood may provide documentation describing usage metrics and reporting. Documentation is provided for convenience and does not modify this Agreement or the Order Form unless expressly incorporated by reference in the Order Form.

### If customer requires binding incorporation
Escalate to Legal + Finance + Engineering.

**Controls if binding incorporation is unavoidable:**
- Incorporate a **specific version/date** (e.g., “Hosted API Meter Definitions v3 dated 2026-02-10”) as an exhibit.
- Make clear that changes require mutual written agreement (or order form amendment).
- Confirm operational ability to continue measuring exactly as described.

---

## Treatment of known edge cases (guidance for negotiations)
Use these positions to keep contracts consistent with platform behavior and internal controls.

1) **Streaming partial completions:** Charge for tokens generated/delivered prior to cancellation/disconnect, subject to product behavior. Do not promise “no charge if customer didn’t receive final token.”

2) **Client-side timeouts:** If the model has begun processing and produced tokens, usage may be incurred. Customers should set timeouts appropriately and use idempotency keys / retry controls.

3) **Server-side errors / 5xx:** Avoid a strict contractual promise of “no charge for 5xx.” Instead: “may be incurred; credits for confirmed service errors or measurement defects under support terms.”

4) **Retries:** Ensure contract language acknowledges that retries can incur additional usage. Encourage customers to use recommended retry/backoff and idempotency patterns.

5) **Console vs invoice differences:** Contract should explicitly state that console reports are informational; invoice is authoritative.

6) **Model aliases / model upgrades:** Avoid pinning a contract to marketing model names. If customers need stability, address via technical controls (model version pinning) and order form language, not metering language.

---

## Escalation and approvals
- Any deviation from the approved clause set, including dispute window >45 days, binding documentation incorporation, custom rounding commitments, or “no-charge for failures” commitments, requires:
  - **Legal (Sofia Mendes or Michael Grant)**
  - **Finance (Laura Bennett or delegate; Billing Controls: Emily Stone)**
  - **Engineering confirmation** when language touches implementation (Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman; Billing hooks: Cole Summers)

For active invoice disputes, follow the **Billing Discrepancy Triage Runbook** and do not negotiate contract amendments as a substitute for operational resolution.

---

- **2026-02-14:** Updated streaming/retries language to align with ADR-027 and metering reconciliation findings; added guidance for binding incorporation controls.
- **2026-01-22:** Initial publication of templates for MSA + Order Form; standardized 30-day dispute window and limited billing audit right.
